about.title: Loma Linda Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a traffic collision in Loma Linda takes a loved one's life, the days that follow can feel impossible to navigate. San Bernardino County records show real people are hurt every year on roads like Barton Road, Redlands Boulevard, and Mountain View Avenue, and occasionally those crashes turn fatal. California law gives certain family members, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, the right to pursue a wrongful death claim, with other dependents or heirs eligible in some situations. These claims are separate from any criminal proceeding and exist to help surviving family members recover funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and compensation for the loss of a loved one's guidance, companionship, and care. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we simply help Loma Linda families connect with an independent attorney who can walk through what applies to their specific circumstances, free of charge and without any obligation.

whyChoose.title: Why Loma Linda Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to specific people, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, with other dependents or heirs sometimes eligible. An independent attorney can help clarify where your family fits before any deadline passes.

items.title: A Firm Two-Year Window
items.desc: California generally requires a wrongful death claim be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks significantly if a government entity was involved. Connecting with an attorney early helps protect your family's ability to pursue the claim at all.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral and burial costs and lost financial support, along with compensation for the loss of a loved one's love, companionship, and guidance. An attorney can help explain how these categories might apply to your specific loss.

items.question: Who in my family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law generally gives first priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children. If none of those exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing to file. An independent attorney can review your family's situation and explain where you stand.

items.question: How long do we have to file after a fatal crash in Loma Linda?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives families two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. That period is shorter if a government agency, such as a public road authority, may bear responsibility. Because Loma Linda sits along corridors like I-10 and Barton Road where public infrastructure can be a factor, it's worth confirming the applicable deadline as soon as possible.

items.question: Does a criminal case against the driver affect our civil claim?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil matter from any criminal charges the driver may face. Your family can pursue compensation through a civil claim regardless of the outcome, or existence, of a criminal case. An attorney can help you understand how the two processes might interact in your specific situation.

items.question: What does LawProactive actually do for grieving families?
items.answer: LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney in your area; we are not a law firm ourselves. There's no cost to speak with an attorney through us, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there's a recovery. Our goal is simply to help Loma Linda families find guidance during an incredibly difficult time.
